The 20 row names, dates, registerUrl and title are the real stored wofford records, and through origin/main's parser this file reproduces all 20 of them identically on (name, startDate, endDate), so it is a faithful model of what main saw. The SPORT HEADINGS are assumed, because nobody has seen the page - and they are what the prediction turns on. rowsEvidence._note: Issue #80 item 1. A row whose name came from the page rather than from the row is gated on the text it was assembled from, because its name carries no sport and no gender for the two unconditional rules to read. ONE rule reads it: the SPORT rule, over `evidence`, the row's whole window. There is deliberately no gender rule on evidence - two cuts of one were tried and both removed. Over the whole window it turned the three `true` window-bleed rows below false, deleting real girls' camps. Bounded to the row's own heading and date lines it changed no fixture at all, was pinned by this group's third case alone, and opened two over-rejection channels that are regressions against pre-#80 main: a 'Men's' token on a row's own date line, and a lower-case heading merged in by _starts_new_row donating its gender token into the row's own lines. Each case names the input that makes it fail: drop the evidence branch and every `false` row below turns true, which is what origin/main does with harvard; add a gender rule over `evidence` and the three `true` window-bleed rows turn false. The `named: row` cases pin that a row with a name of its own is judged on the name alone, evidence or no evidence, so nothing tightens for the 129 rows that were never the problem.

newRow._note: Issue #80 item 1, the chimera. The date lookahead used to stop only at a line naming a camp or a clinic, so harvard's lacrosse row ran on into a basketball row that uses neither word and took its date. A continuation carries the date and nothing else, or a label in front of it; its own record carries a name: two or more CAPITALISED words once a leading label is stripped. The first cut counted [A-Za-z]{2,}, which is case blind, and 7 of 20 ordinary prose continuations became their own record - 'Check in begins June 6, 2026', 'Rain date: June 7, 2026', 'Cost $350 due by June 1, 2026' - each of which is a date a row then never picks up, or a truncated detail window. Those seven are the `false` cases below and they are the input that makes the case-blind version fail. Each `true` case is an input that makes the pre-#80 guard fail, so the tightening cannot quietly become a condition that never fires.

pageName._note: Issue #80 item 5. _page_camp_name reads a name out of the opening lines of a page whose own title is chrome. It takes the first CAMP_PHRASE_RE candidate it finds, so without a sanity check it adopts whatever that phrase names. The name is read FIRST and unconditionally by _row_allowed, so a boys' or another sport's page name rejects every page-named row on the page; and where rows survive, the repair stamps that name onto them and #78's classifier reads it as its only input. The guard is that the candidate must itself pass _row_allowed. Each `null` case below is an input that makes the unguarded version adopt a name that is worse than the chrome title it replaces.
